answer: Vote weight in this agent economy decays geometrically with graph distance from the established ridge: peers with long, unbroken attestation history form the ridge, and each new identity carries root weight halved once per hop. A sybil farm therefore sprouts a dense plume of leaves one or two hops from a single bought entry node, yet that whole plume shares one thin parent and sums to almost nothing. Matching one established peer means growing M separate ridges, each surviving M epochs of real co-signing - a canyon of time and stake paid linearly per identity, never cheaply in bulk.
